content:
Marco: kicking off Pulumi/Terraform work for a eu-central-2 region bring-up. I have modules sketched for network, iam, eks/gke-like cluster shim, and a dedicated gpu pool. need quick review on state backend + CI wiring before i open the PR.

Sophia: thanks Marco — quick q: are you leaning Pulumi or Terraform for the region modules? we should pick one for consistency (prefer Pulumi for app infra but TF still used in a few landing zones).

Marco: leaning Pulumi for new stuff, but we need a Terraform backend compatibility story (some older state lives in TF). plan: Pulumi for new modules, but persist state into S3 (or GCS) with locking so both tools can interop at the state level when we migrate.

Riley: +1 on Pulumi for new modules. for cross-tool state, keep separate keys/prefixes. also need dynamodb table for TF locking if we ever run terraform for bootstrapping.

Anya: pinging infra-ops checklist: do we have quota requests in for eu-central-2 GPUs? which instance families? i will follow up with cloud ops.

Marco: current plan: request 12 x a10g + 6 x h100 across two AZs as initial pool. i created a ticket to request quotas (cloud ticket #3821). DevOps Bot: performed an availability & quota scan earlier today.

DevOps Bot: AWS region eu-central-2: GPU instance types a10g/h100 available = yes; default vCPU quota for region = 1024; GPUs quota (per instance family) = 0 -> request required. created draft quota request in console.

Sophia: good. on state wiring: sample terraform backend i recommend (keeps locking/consistency):

```
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "redwood-terraform-state"
    key            = "eu-central-2/infrastructure.tfstate"
    region         = "eu-central-2"
    dynamodb_table = "tf-state-lock"
    encrypt        = true
  }
}
```

Sophia: and for Pulumi, use the S3 login + KMS encryption and store stack metadata under `pulumi/eu-central-2`. e.g.:

```
pulumi login s3://redwood-pulumi-state/eu-central-2
pulumi stack init redwood/eu-central-2/prod
pulumi config set aws:region eu-central-2 --stack redwood/eu-central-2/prod
```

Marco: CI wiring proposal: GitHub Actions runs `pulumi preview`/`pulumi up` in two-step flow. plan: run preview on PR (always), require codeowner approval for apply, run apply in protected branch via `workflow_dispatch` or `repo & env` approvals. creds via short-lived OIDC tokens. snippet: 

```
# actions/pulumi.yml (excerpt)
- name: Pulumi Preview
  run: pulumi preview --stack redwood/eu-central-2/prod
  env:
    PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PULUMI_CFG_PASSPHRASE }}

- name: Pulumi Up (manual)
  if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
  run: pulumi up --yes --stack redwood/eu-central-2/prod
  env:
    AWS_ROLE_ARN: ${{ secrets.EU_CENTRAL_DEPLOY_ROLE }}
```

Riley: prefer OIDC: use `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` -> assume role; avoid long-lived secrets. enforce PR protection: require 2 reviewers + infra codeowner.

Anya: validation checklist to include in runbook before handoff:
- VPC subnets (public/private) created and annotated
- Route tables + NAT gateways validated
- Security groups for GPU pool (SSH limited, control-plane ports only)
- IAM roles for node pools + service accounts with least privilege
- KMS keys for state buckets enabled with rotation
- Remote state encryption + locking verified
- Peering / Transit Gateway routes to prod region tested (if needed)
- GPU quota confirmed and allocation ticket closed
- Cost estimate + tagging policy applied (billing tags: team, env, cost-center)

Marco: adding health checks: after apply run these quick checks:
- `aws ec2 describe-instances` for GPU instances `--filters Name=instance-type,Values=a10g,h100`
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` ensure GPU nodes have `nvidia.com/gpu` allocatable
- e2e inference smoke job (docker image `redwood/gpu-smoke:latest`) deploy to node pool, run sample 1k-token generation, assert latency < 150ms baseline

Sophia: also add automatic rollback policy: if cluster autoscaler fails or GPU node drain rate > X% in 10m, route traffic back to fallback region (we have traffic routing via smart-router). document expected failure modes in runbook.

Riley: small CI detail: when pulumi uses S3 backend we must ensure backend bucket lifecycle + retention for state snapshots (30d) and CSP audit logs exported. also add `pulumi stack export` artifact on every apply to the artifacts bucket.

Anya: handoff notes for oncall:
- Primary owner: Marco (pager-duty team infra-gpu)
- Secondary: Riley
- Runbook link: /docs/infra/region-bringup/eu-central-2 (will add once PR merged)
- Post-apply checklist to run within 1h: network validation, security scan, smoke inference job

Marco: i'll open PR with modules + CI workflows. will include a `docs/runbook.md` in the repo with the above checklist and the validation commands. can reviewers please verify the backend config, iam policy snippets, and the apply gating?

Sophia: i'll review today. look out for a few tweaks on IAM least-privilege and KMS key policy. :+1:

Riley: i'll validate the quota ticket once PR is up and coordinate capacity allocation with cloud provider.

DevOps Bot: PR template check: missing `changelog` label and `security-review` flag.

Anya: acked. i can draft the handoff page after PR merge.

Marco: thanks all — will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
